items.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You know, when we‘d meet in town, I‘d go see her, she‘d come see me.

ctx.x: Oh, Sarah‘s a sweetheart. Last time Sarah was in town . . . she was here right before she passed, too. Damn. So I went by to see her. She was at Charley‘s, lived down there, and I said, ―You coming over the house tonight when you get done?‖ ―You got some food?‖ I said, ―Yeah.‖ And I had fixed a lot of food, you know. I remembered she liked meatloaf, so I had that fixed, but I had other stuff I had to heat up. Well, she got into the meatloaf right away. ―Give me a piece of bread. I‘m starving to death. I lost ten…

I say, ―Where?‖ And she ate and ate and ate, and I had a couple of people; Bill Harris was here, and Fanny and a couple of musicians. So when she got through eating she came to the piano. The piano‘s right here, and she came in and she played, and it was right down there. She started playing. I said, ―Don‘t nobody say a word.‖ She played and sang, and I couldn‘t get my machine. I wanted to push the button to record this. I guess maybe it wasn‘t meant for me to. I couldn‘t get that button, that damn thing to work,…
